title: Federal Judge Demands 30-Day Notice After Trump Hints at Kennedy Center Demolition
snippet: A federal judge has ordered the Trump administration to give a 30-day warning before taking any steps to alter or demolish the historic Kennedy Center, following remarks by the president suggesting the landmark could be 'ripped down.'
content:
WASHINGTON — A federal judge has ordered the Trump administration to provide at least 30 days' advance notice before taking any action to demolish or alter the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, adding a new layer of judicial oversight to an escalating battle over the iconic Washington venue.

U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper issued the directive on Thursday in response to recent public remarks by President Donald Trump. Speaking to reporters in North Carolina, Trump suggested that the arts landmark could end up being "ripped down" if his administration is not given recognition on the building's facade.

A Mounting Dispute Over Renovation and Naming Rights

The legal clash stems from an ongoing lawsuit filed by Rep. Joyce Beatty, D-Ohio, who serves as an ex officio member of the center's board. Beatty has repeatedly challenged attempts to place Trump's name on the memorial, arguing that only Congress holds the authority to rename the facility established in 1971 in honor of President John F. Kennedy.

Tensions spiked this week after the board, stacked with Trump appointees, voted to temporarily close the facility for up to two years to conduct a $257 million renovation. Executive Director Matt Floca cited structural safety concerns as the cause for immediate access restrictions, but critics contend the prolonged closure is a maneuver to force changes without oversight.

While Judge Cooper declined to grant Beatty's request for an emergency hearing on the closure, his order ensures that any potential physical alterations to the venue will require prior court notification. The administration is expected to file further motions seeking to lift existing operating restrictions to proceed with repairs.
